summary: Dagfinn Føllesdal (1932–2026) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Oslo and Harvard University, where he studied under Willard Van Orman Quine in 1961. He held posts at the University of Oslo (~1967–1999) and Stanford University (~1968–2010).
Dagmar Schwerk works in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Hamburg (~2005–2017) under her doctoral supervisor Dorji Wangchuk (~2012–2017).
Daijo Tokiwa (1870–1945) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1896 to 1899 and held an academic post at Toyo University from ~1904 to 1939.

Daiju Sasaki (born 1977) is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Taisho University (~1996–2007). In 2015, he was attested as a part-time lecturer at Taisho University and a full-time lecturer at Chisan Denpoin.

Dainin Katagiri (1928–1990) was a Buddhist studies figure who founded the Minnesota Zen Meditation Center. He studied at Komazawa University (~1948–1952) and trained under traditional teacher Eko Hashimoto (~1946–1953).

Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki (1870–1966) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying under Kosen Imakita, Soen Shaku, and Paul Carus. He held posts at Tokyo Imperial University, Otani University (~1921–1960), and Columbia University (~1952–1957).

Daishun Ueyama (1934–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Akira Fujieda (~1958–1963). He held posts at Ryukoku University as an assistant professor (~1970–1976) and as president in 1983.

Dale S. Wright (born 1948) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, having studied under Alan Anderson, Wang Pachow, and Robert Scharlemann. From ~1980 to 2016, he served as a professor of religious and Asian studies at Occidental College.

Dalsukh D. Malvania (1910–2000) was a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held a post at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1951) and served as Director of the L.D. Institute of Indology (attested 1965–1971).
Damdin Badaraev is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and linguistics. He studied under Bidya Dandaron and George Roerich.

Damien Keown (born 1951) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who earned his BA at Lancaster University and doctoral degree at Oxford. He founded the Journal of Buddhist Ethics and served at Goldsmiths, University of London.

Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi (1907–1966) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Cambridge Rindge and Latin School, Harvard University (~1924–1929), and Fergusson College, later holding a post at Banaras Hindu University (~1930–1931).

Dan Arnold (born 1965) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, earning a PhD from the University of Chicago (~1993–2002). He held posts at McGill University (~2001–2003), the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, and the University of Chicago (~2003).

Dan Lusthaus (born 1950) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy, earning his Ph.D. from Temple University. He held posts at Grinnell College, Bates College, Macalester College, Florida State University, the University of Georgia, and Harvard University.

Dan Martin (born 1953) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his Ph.D. at Indiana University (~1985–1991). He held posts at the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and Carnegie Mellon University.

Dan Smyer Yü works in religious studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD from the University of California, Davis, and served as a Research Group Leader at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity.

Dan Zahavi (born 1967) is a philosopher who earned his PhD at KU Leuven (~1990–1994) and his Habilitation at the University of Copenhagen (~1995–1999). In ~2002, he became Professor of Philosophy at the University of Copenhagen.

Daniel A. Getz works in Sinology and Buddhist studies, earning a PhD from Yale University under Stanley Weinstein (attested 1994). He served as an associate professor at Bradley University (attested 2019).

Daniel Aitken is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD from the University of Tasmania, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Jay L. Garfield, and also studied under Parimal G. Patil and Leonard van der Kuijp.
Daniel Amadé Scheidegger specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his doctoral degree from the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.
